Since you just want this done right now in PowerShell, here is the exact command you can copy and paste into your PowerShell terminal to instantly clip out a random 15-second snippet (starting at 10 minutes in) without any quality loss:

```powershell
& 'C:\Users\renu5\Downloads\nishe found\ffmpeg\ffmpeg.exe' -ss 00:10:00 -i 'C:\Users\renu5\Downloads\clipping\cliping first video\TNE with Louisa Nicola, Keith Rabois episode (1).mp4' -t 00:00:15 -c copy 'C:\Users\renu5\Downloads\clipping\cliping first video\viral_pipeline\random_clip.mp4' -y
```

**What this does:**
1. `-ss 00:10:00`: Skips right to the 10-minute mark.
2. `-t 00:00:15`: Clips out exactly 15 seconds.
3. `-c copy`: Copies the stream directly without re-encoding, meaning it takes a fraction of a second to complete!

Just hit enter on that and your `random_clip.mp4` will instantly appear in your `viral_pipeline` folder. Let me know if you want me to adjust the timestamps!
